name: design_pattern_retrofits
description:
Build benchmark.json and benchmark_lite.json from all prior mining efforts.

Every task is one design-pattern instance with two project states that are
equivalent in external behavior:

* ``pattern``    -- the code contains the pattern instance.
* ``no_pattern`` -- the code does not (pre-retrofit history, or a synthesized
  reversal on a branch/patch).

``subtasks.apply`` starts from ``no_pattern`` and should reach ``pattern``;
``subtasks.remove`` starts from ``pattern`` and should reach ``no_pattern``.
A subtask is ``available`` only when its starting state exists.

Run ``python resolve_dpdf.py`` first; then ``python build_benchmark.py``.

verification_levels.manual_case_study_borderline: Hand-reviewed, but the pattern fit is weak.
verification_levels.human_validated: Mined candidate confirmed by a human reviewer.
verification_levels.manual_reversal: Upstream pattern instance with a hand-made reversal branch.
verification_levels.llm_validated: Mined retrofit commit approved by an LLM only.
verification_levels.tool_detected: DPD-F detection, re-located at the latest repository HEAD.

rules.dpdf_structural_check_not_passed: DPD-F hits whose class at the latest HEAD fails (or has no) structural check for its pattern.
rules.llm_analysis_saw_no_code: Tesis-pipeline approvals where the LLM reported it was not shown the code.
rules.remove_target_missing_at_pattern_commit: History tasks whose remove-target class cannot be found at the pattern commit (wrong birth commit or unresolved rename).

mechanic.prompt:
Goal: apply the Builder pattern for creating Table instances by providing a concrete TableBuilder implementation and wiring Connection to return a builder.

Create a new class org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.TableBuilderBase that implements org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.TableBuilder with private final org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.Connection connection and private final org.apache.hadoop.hbase.TableName tableName fields, mutable fields int operationTimeout, rpcTimeout, readRpcTimeout, writeRpcTimeout and long writeBufferSize; add a package-private constructor TableBuilderBase(Connection connection, TableName tableName) that assigns the finals; implement each setter to set the corresponding field and return this; implement build() to delegate to the existing table-creation logic by returning connection.getTable(tableName).

Modify org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.Connection by adding a new method public org.apache.hadoop.hbase.client.TableBuilder getTableBuilder(org.apache.hadoop.hbase.TableName tableName) { return new TableBuilderBase(this, tableName); } and change the existing public Table getTable(TableName tableName) to delegate to getTableBuilder(tableName).build(); (no other API changes).

product_owner.prompt:
Title: Construction/configuration logic embedded in HTable hinders extensibility and maintenance

Description: HTable currently owns construction and configuration state (fields, setters, and constructors), which couples creation to implementation, forces deprecated setters to remain for compatibility, and makes adding new table types or changing config brittle and error-prone. Centralizing creation/configuration into a single construction component will decouple responsibilities, allow producing different table implementations cleanly, and reduce maintenance and testing overhead.

remove.instruction: Remove the Builder pattern implemented by TableBuilder.

context.commit_subject: HBASE-17491 Remove all setters from HTable interface and introduce a TableBuilder to build Table instance
context.justification: This interface is a textbook Builder pattern for constructing a `Table` connection object. Creating a `Table` requires several optional configuration values — operation timeouts, RPC timeouts for reads vs. writes, and request attributes — but a caller usually only wants to tweak one or two of them. Instead of forcing a massive constructor with all possible parameters (which becomes unreadable), the Builder pattern lets a caller chain only the settings it cares about, then call `build()` at the end to get a fully configured `Table`. Each setter (e.g., `setOperationTimeout`, `setReadRpcTimeout`) returns the `TableBuilder` itself, enabling fluent method chaining like `connection.getTableBuilder(tableName, pool).setOperationTimeout(5000).setReadRpcTimeout(2000).build()`. The implementation fills in sensible defaults for anything not explicitly set.

alternatives.prompt:
Remove the Builder pattern from class ClusterMetricsBuilder in file hbase-client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hbase/ClusterMetricsBuilder.java.
Replace the builder with telescoping constructors on the product class.

Steps:
1. Identify the product class that the builder constructs (the class with the private
   constructor accepting the builder). Make its constructor(s) public.
2. Add multiple overloaded public constructors for the most common combinations of
   parameters. Each constructor should delegate to a fully-parameterised one using
   `this(...)`.
3. Delete the ClusterMetricsBuilder builder class (and any inner Builder class) entirely.
4. Find every call site that used the builder (search for `new ClusterMetricsBuilder.Builder`
   or `ClusterMetricsBuilder.builder()` or similar) and replace each with a direct constructor
   call using the appropriate overload.
5. Ensure the product class fields are no longer final if they were set only via the
   builder — or keep them final and ensure all constructors initialise them.

The resulting code should have constructors with 3 or more parameters on the product
class, exhibiting the Long Parameter List code smell.

---
**Verification instructions (follow these exactly):**

After making all changes, verify the code compiles:
   `/app/run_build.sh`
   Fix any compilation errors before continuing.

Remove the Builder pattern from class ClusterMetricsBuilder in file hbase-client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hbase/ClusterMetricsBuilder.java.
Replace the builder with a single all-arguments constructor on the product class.

Steps:
1. Identify the product class and make it have one public constructor accepting
   ALL configuration fields as parameters (including optional ones).
2. For optional parameters that previously had defaults in the builder, use sentinel
   values (e.g. -1 for ints, null for objects) to indicate "use default".
3. Delete the ClusterMetricsBuilder builder class entirely.
4. Update all call sites to invoke the new all-args constructor, passing null or -1
   for parameters they do not wish to configure.

The resulting code should have a single constructor with many parameters exhibiting
the Long Parameter List code smell, with callers forced to pass sentinel/null values.

mechanic.prompt:
Goal: apply the Decorator pattern to Resource by introducing an abstract ResourceDecorator that wraps a single Resource, delegates all read/inspection methods to it and disables mutation methods.

Create a new file src/main/org/apache/tools/ant/types/resources/ResourceDecorator.java in package org.apache.tools.ant.types.resources that declares "public abstract class ResourceDecorator extends Resource" with a private Resource resource field, protected no-arg constructor, and protected ResourceDecorator(ResourceCollection other) that calls addConfigured(other); add public final void addConfigured(ResourceCollection a) which enforces checkChildrenAllowed(), single-element collection and assigns the wrapped resource; add protected final Resource getResource() which dereferences references (isReference/getCheckedRef) and throws BuildException if no resource; override public void setRefid(Reference r) to throw if resource != null then call super; implement delegation methods getName(), isExists(), getLastModified(), isDirectory(), getSize(), getInputStream(), getOutputStream(), public Object as(Class clazz), public boolean isFilesystemOnly() returning as(FileProvider.class) != null, public int compareTo(Object other) delegating to wrapped resource, public int hashCode(), and dieOnCircularReference(Stack, Project) that checks references and delegates to the wrapped resource; and add mutation-disabling methods setName(String), setExists(boolean), setLastModified(long), setDirectory(boolean), setSize(long) that always throw BuildException.  

Add necessary imports: java.io.InputStream, java.io.IOException, java.io.OutputStream, java.util.Stack and org.apache.tools.ant.BuildException, org.apache.tools.ant.Project, org.apache.tools.ant.types.Resource, org.apache.tools.ant.types.Reference, org.apache.tools.ant.types.ResourceCollection; no existing classes need to be moved or renamed.
